title: Large complex meshes lay out as mostly 1x1 patches: too many cones and zero arcs on scan-scale input
user-messages: I am not so concerned about this, log a follow up ticket about large complex meshes having mostly 1x1 patches
description: On the Trellis T-Rex skull (C:/Blends/Dinos/T-RexSkullModel/3d/ComfyUI_00028.glb, ~700k faces, genus 24) quad_layout completes (CRAW-114) with 31,841 quads but 29,961 patches: 29,464 patches (98%) are a single quad, only 109 have more than 4. The seamless UV unit is 1% of the bounding-box diagonal and target_edge_length defaults to 1.0, so the quad size is sensible; the patches are tiny because the layout is too complex: 1,020 cones, 116,716 arcs of which 55,130 quantize to zero length. A patch layout of mostly 1x1 patches is no segmentation. Find where the cones come from on noisy scan-scale meshes and reduce them the way the papers intend (cross-field smoothness, curvature bias, KCP13 / BZK09 / LCK21a), so large meshes get patches spanning many quads. Related: PATCH-47 (spurious singularities on noisy meshes, older simplified solver).
definition-of-done:
1. On the T-Rex skull the layout's patches average well above one quad each, with the cone count explained against the paper the fix follows.
2. Every suite model (bolt buddha feline hand sphere_base block botijo elk fertility rockerarm fandisk) keeps a valid layout; any change in its patch count is reported.
3. Build checkstyle-green; touched tests pass.
testing-plan:
1. Run the skull DSL (load_mesh, repair_mesh, quad_layout) and report cones, arcs, zero arcs, patches and the quads-per-patch histogram before and after.
2. Run the 11-model suite and compare quads, patches and cones.
changes-made: Archived 2026-11-22 without landing, as tag archive/craw-120 at 5ea14b8c: Cones on the skull are real geometry; no cross-field setting from KCP13, BZK09 or LCK21a cuts them by more than 18%. The smoothestField fix it found landed via PATCH-123. Open options not taken: alpha 30 deg plus the pinched-patch fix, or BZK09 section 5.3 cone relocation.
